name: Barn to Basket
notes:
We're building local communities around a healthier, less expensive approach to feeding our families.

Why?
Our "why" is a pretty simple one. We've watched the demand for our direct product increase as our neighbors in town saw grocery prices going WAY UP, and grocery store quality going WAY DOWN.

Our mission?
Connect the many small farms across this incredible country with their neighbors "in town". We believe that with just a little effort, we can feed families and build healthy communities around a very simple, very neighborly exchange.

Who is Barn to Basket for?
Barn to Basket is for everyone. We've all got to eat, and if we get Barn to Basket right, we can all eat healthy, fresh food while strengthening our communities and demonstrating the sustainability of community supported agriculture.

name: Rye Resurgence Project
notes:
The Rye Resurgence Project is a women-founded, grassroots effort to build the market for San Luis Valley-grown rye in order to restore area aquifers, improve soil health, and secure a sustainable future for this historic and vital agricultural region of Colorado. The RRP represents a collective of 10 San Luis Valley farmers growing high-alpine rye and works with millers, bakers, brewers, distillers, chefs, and other partners in Colorado’s food and beverage economy to craft unique rye goods that in turn enhance public knowledge, appreciation, and desire for this environmentally-beneficial, local grain. 

All RRP farmers grow rye with minimal water usage to dramatically reduce reliance on groundwater and preserve the Rio Grande, and as a winter cover crop, the rye grown also advances soil retention, reducing area dust storms and improving soil nutrients. Whether grown with minimal-to-no intervention, Organic Certified, or Regenerative Organic Certified, Resurgence Rye grown by our farmers utilizes regenerative agricultural practices. In the first full year of the project, RRP farmers planted 4,500 acres of winter rye, resulting in a total annual water savings of 4,670 acre-feet.

Everything is made in a licensed commercial kitchen with a strong focus on safe handling, clean production, and dependable quality, so customers can feel confident with every bite.

What makes my business special is the meaning behind it. As a Peruvian immigrant, baking alfajores became my way of sharing “home” in a place that was once new to me; turning memories, tradition, and comfort into something people can taste. I care about the little details: thoughtful packaging, a warm customer experience, and a product that feels both familiar and exciting for anyone trying it for the first time.

I’m grateful for every person who supports a small business, and I truly love meeting customers face-to-face at local markets. Those moments, watching someone take a bite, hearing their stories, and seeing cultures connect, are the reason I do this.

name: Boulder Valley School District
notes:
Boulder Valley School District's School Food Project makes high quality school food with an emphasis on clean labels and local food.  We serve over 15,000 meals each day.  We use healthier, locally sourced, and organic ingredients whenever possible, and we avoid highly processed foods, high fructose corn syrup, chemicals, dyes and food additives.

All of our beef and chicken on the bone and nacho meat is hormone- and antibiotic-free and our bulk milk is local and natural. Salad Bars are offered daily at every school and are stocked with fresh, delicious and when possible, local farm fresh produce.

Our interactive food and nutrition education programs make eating healthy food fun for students of all ages. Through our programs, BVSD kids learn where food comes from, what fresh food tastes like, and even how to grow and cook their own food.

Our food is prepared in our 33,591-square-foot facility, then is shipped daily to schools for finishing.  The Culinary Center features a loading dock with a fresh food processing area for deliveries, three food prep areas, abundant storage, a blast chill area, and business spaces. Features such as precise temperature control and separate areas for preparing raw meat and fresh veggies promote food safety.  Production of food at one location provides more control over quality and waste.

name: Empirical Genetics LLC
notes:
Empirical Genetics is a hemp breeding company that sells hemp planting seed, and grows hemp fiber & hemp grain for food.  We utilize sustainable farming practices, incorporating cattle grazing to increase soil health and biodiversity in the soil, which increases organic matter and in turn increases soil water retention. This culminates in a decreased need for added fertilizer each year and ultimately, decreasing salinity levels in the soil & water system from runoff to water ways and the water table as a whole, supporting the Colorado River Basin Salinity Control Program. We believe with the data we are in the process of collecting this year and in the future, we will be significantly impacting the high concentrations of salinity in Colorado water.

Empirical Genetics primary activity is using our industrial hemp planting seed and this year's fiber crop to develop and validate our methods of carbon sequestration and the quantification of the actual CO2 sequestered from the atmosphere instead of the arbitrary equations that are currently in use. This is the proof of concept model that can be used for all other commodity crops. The same methods used to get a homogenized/representative sample of silage corn for quantification of protein has been implemented in our harvested hemp fiber and food grain sampling process for the quantification of carbon sequestered in the soil and harvested hemp crop.

This is going to be done by taking the homogenized representative industrial hemp sample and conducting an Ash Test measuring Total Carbon analysis by utilizing an SH Scientific Laboratory Muffle Furnace. In addition, the furnace will be utilized to measure Total Inorganic Mineral Content in the soil. Utilizing our methods of carbon quantification, we will be producing a validated scale ticket, by measuring the carbon sequestered from the hemp at the grain elevator. By doing this we are creating a whole new category of value added to the agricultural carbon smart commodities.

The current quantification utilized by carbon registry, carbon sequestration certification, and carbon sequestration programs operated by large agricultural corporations are based on inaccurate and out of date equations. These corporations are paying farmers a fraction of the value of the carbon offsets from the carbon sequestered from their land, and their opaque calculations are putting the farmers at a significant financial disadvantage. Even worse, these practices are restricting the adoption of climate smart commodities and general acceptance of the validity of carbon sequestration. This hinders the overall growth of this sector. 

This foundational hemp carbon sequestration information will be used as an anchor to create correlating data for quantifiable accurate carbon sequestration by cattle grazing.

Little h Farm is a small, growing hobby farm raising Hares, Hens, Hogs, and Honeybees — the “little h’s” that inspired our name.
After starting with rabbits, we expanded to chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys, and pigs. We always try to do best by our animals while also knowing them as nourishment for our bodies. A like-minded friend once told me, "it's nice to know that the animal you are eating was loved."
Little h Farm came upon soap making as a bit of an accident. We started raising animals years ago because we believe in knowing where our food comes from and in humane treatment of animals. After taking our hogs to the processor in 2025, they called and asked if we wanted the fat. I said "yes" with some hesitancy. Yes because I want every part of the animal to be used if possible. Hesitancy because I didn't know what to do with it. After doing some research I landed on soap making. This was a useful and practical product out of our own lard. After making the first couple of batches I was hooked. I loved making soap: blending the essential oils, researching natural products to create beautiful colors, and working with the materials to bring it all together. Bonus: this soap is amazingly moisturizing, soft and silky on skin, and smells great!

Our tasty cookies have deep Belgian roots! With Belgian ancestry on both sides of my family tree, I grew up surrounded by rich traditions, but richest of all was our family's lukken cookie recipe, producing crispy, buttery, delicious cookies with a hint of whiskey flavor. My great-great-grandmother, Flavie Dewaele, emigrated from Belgium with the recipe, making her cookies one-by-one with an iron heated over a wood stove. We still use Flavie's original recipe today and I have fond memories of gathering in my grandparent's home each November to produce thousands of Belgian cookies to gift to our family and friends for the holidays.

We went from tradition to business during the holiday season of 2021-2022, bringing Belgian lukken cookies to markets along Colorado's Front Range. It's been a treat to see how many people enjoy these special cookies. "Lukken" means "to succeed" in Dutch, so from my family to yours, we wish you luck and love with every box!

name: kingrestaurantcolorado
notes:
In the heat of Mand Mour, Punjab, brothers Tirlochn and Paramjit Mand harbored a shared dream – to transplant the vibrant flavors of Punjabi cuisine to the United States. Fueled by their elder brother's successful example, they embarked on this ambitious journey in 1992. Packed with determination, they boarded a plane, their minimal luggage a testament to their unwavering resolve. Arriving at their elder brother's restaurant marked the start of their journey. For the next four years, they navigated the intricate tapestry of American life, honing their skills in cooking, cleaning, and the nuances of restaurant operations. This transformative experience not only developed business experience but also underscored the profound importance of disseminating Punjabi culture in the heart of America.



Having learned all there was to master about operating a restaurant, Tirlochn and Paramjit decided to forge their path by opening their own establishment – the inaugural King Restaurant in Fishers, Indiana. The launch garnered attention, yet despite initial excitement, the restaurant faced closure within six months due to minimal traction. Rather than viewing this as a setback, however, the brothers viewed it as another pivotal step in their journey, a valuable lesson that would shape their future endeavors. Undeterred, they carried this wisdom with them as they relocated to Minnesota. In November 2003, a mere two months after settling in, Tirlochn and Paramjit seized an opportunity to apply the lessons from their past venture and founded India Palace in Eden Prairie.



This time, the brothers not only ensured that word of their restaurant reverberated across town, but they also strategized to sustain traction well beyond the initial days. Actively engaging with the community, catering events, and crafting sumptuous dishes, they aimed to capture the hearts of Eden Prairie's residents. Soon, their culinary offerings became synonymous with Punjabi culture in Minnesota, transforming their restaurant into a cherished sanctuary. Two decades later, the Mand brothers have blossomed into a culinary empire, boasting ten restaurants under the Mand family name. From Punjab, India, to Eden Prairie, Minnesota, and now spanning Texas, Minnesota, North Dakota, and Colorado, they have evolved into a symbolic force of Punjabi culture and cuisine, bringing vibrancy to the plates and lives of all who savor their delicious creations

name: Mile High Mycro Farms
notes:
In April 2021, I started Mile High Mycro Farms with the idea of being able to offer the community a healthy, organic array of microgreens, vegetables, and mushrooms in a sustainable, responsible way. 
Here at Mile High Mycro Farms, I believe that how you do anything, is how you do everything, and when it comes to feeding your community, there’s only one way to do it, the right way. 
If you ask us to define “the right way” we believe that means keeping it simple: non-GMO, all organic seeds, grown in the most sustainable way possible.
Ensuring they are free of any pesticides, herbicides, or any other chemicals is a top priority, not only to ensure the quality of products, but to sustain the operation by composting all of our organic green waste into the best soil possible for raised beds.
By offering our community healthy, fresh, nutritious foods, I believe we can empower all people to grow to their fullest potential. As an LGBTQ+ owned business, I aspire to invest in the community and help to build a happier, healthier world, for everyone.
As my farm grows, I look forward to seeing how it is able to serve our community in a way that makes a positive impact.

At an elevation of 5,400 feet, the warm summer days and cool nights combine with a fertile soil to provide ideal growing conditions. From a modest beginning the farm has grown to 14 acres of field and orchard production with an additional 13,000 square feet of colorful flowers, organic herbs and vegetable plants in our greenhouses.

Our fresh, organic fruit and vegetables are hand picked in the field at the peak of flavor and nutritional value. Their beauty and great taste are a treat to the pallette and a pleasure to prepare. We offer a wide selection of gourmet and heirloom vegetables and are best known for the amazing sweet taste of our famous "Bordens' Best" homegrown tomatoes and our sweet, juicy peaches.

During the season our premium hanging baskets, fruit, vegetables and herbs are available through our CSA program and at Farmers Markets or our farm stands in Aspen, Carbondale, Edwards, Ridgway, Montrose, Telluride, and Crested Butte.

name: Blue Shed Urban Gardens, LLC
notes:

I want to make my business self-sustaining and do this through a spring seedling sale, selling a portion (about 25%) of my produce/baked goods/jams/simple syrups and hosting events. As a retired firefighter from the Colorado Springs Fire Department, Bob Burton understands the value of perseverance and unbridled passion. Bob has been helping fellow Coloradans with their cattle for years. And eventually, he decided to turn that passion into action when he started his own ranch. What began with just six cattle is now a widely successful cattle company in Divide, Colorado with hundreds of cows and yaks.

As a family-run cattle company, PBJ Cattle Company is all about treating everyone like family — especially our cows and yaks. PBJ Cattle Company utilizes Temple Grandin humane practices to ensure that all of our cows and yaks are treated with respect and cared for properly.

And the result? Higher quality beef for you and your family. Our high-altitude grass-fed beef is not only packed with more flavor, but also with more nutrition. High-altitude grass diets produce less fat and more protein, resulting in healthier meat on your dinner plate. Not only that, but our cows and yaks are never pumped with harmful hormones or steroids of any kind. They also never experience serious spikes of adrenaline. That means your beef will always be free of hormones, steroids, and adrenaline.

Less stress and additives mean more nutrition and more flavor. What more could you ask for?

name: Gardens of Fire
notes:
We are a veteran owned biochar producer in Durango, Co. We produce our own biochar for our farm from locally sourced firewood slash derived from standing dead beetle kill (ponderosa pine). Our company focuses on end-to-end biochar in a low tech and regenerative manner.  Not only do we produce high quality biochar with our flamecap kilns, but we produce it with an extremely low carbon footprint and work with our clients or local projects to install it. 

We provide a surplus of our biochar to our local community at the farmer's market. Our focus and strategy are to empower more citizens and farmers to come together and produce biochar for their communities to improve soil health in a long-term manner.  Biochar education is a passion of ours, and we host workshops throughout the year where we share the basics around biochar. 

Beyond selling our surplus biochar, we also focus on finding farmers in our community who know about biochar but can not afford it. We partner with them and train them to produce their own at an affordable rate. This alleviates the unaffordability aspect of biochar and instead lets them be involved in the production process where they can eventually intake these skills provide an internal input that can lower their year over year fertilizer and water costs.

name: Muriel L MacGregor Charitable Trust | MacGregor Ranch
notes:
Nestled in the beautiful Black Canyon Creek area of Estes Park, our Ranch has remained a showplace of early life among settlers and homesteaders in Colorado Territory.
 
Founded in 1873 by Alexander and Clara MacGregor the Ranch then passed to their son, Donald, and his wife, Maude, and finally, to their only child, Muriel Lurilla MacGregor.  Muriel left her ranch in a trust after her death in 1970 to be preserved as an active cattle ranch with net proceeds from the ranch and cattle operations to be used for charitable or educational purposes.  

MacGregor beef is 100% grass fed and grass finished. Allowed to graze and grow naturally, with no additional hormones or steroids, on lush pastures and high mountain meadows, our cattle are worth the wait! They are no doubt in high demand and limited quantity, so we encourage you to place your order early. Processing dates available in January and June each year.  
Enjoy responsibly raised beef and take the opportunity to learn more about our methods on the Ranch. 

Visit the MacGregor Ranch and tour our historic area, a nationally registered historic site, and our museum, created in one of the original MacGregor homes built in 1896.  Explore the home of the three generations of MacGregor's who settled, homesteaded, and developed the land to become the Ranch that provided for their family and the town. Built in the 1800's the MacGregor's facilitated many avenues of growth for the town of Estes Park and its other influential members. 
Tour the historic homestead June through October each year, and discover history never gets old. 
​

ReKaivery’s food hubs will provide a space for local farmers to sell on consignment and allow consumers to conveniently shop local products six days a week, without traveling far to do so. In partnership and in proximity to local farmers' markets, ReKaivery will be closed while the market is open, encouraging consumers to purchase products directly from the farmer. We collaborate, not compete. 

For farmers, ReKaivery is not your typical retailer, either. ReKaivery will sell food on consignment, ensuring farmers have full ownership of their food and autonomy over their prices. This helps farmers achieve more equitable returns compared to wholesale models. As a future SNAP retailer, this also opens farmers to a bigger customer base.

We believe everyone should know who grows their food, and the farmer will be at the forefront of the ReKaivery shopping experience. Accompanying the farmers’ space will be information to educate and connect consumers to who they’re buying from; the farm’s branding, location, story, and distance away from the hub (food mileage) will be on display. Shopping local should be convenient. It should be equitable. It should be fulfilling. ReKaivery is setting out to make food shopping a better experience for all. Launching April 2022.

name: VanWinkle Ranch
notes:
Our Story
The VanWinkles are 4th and 5th generation ranchers focused on beef production who also know the importance of caring for the land, livestock, and community.
Howard and Janie first met in their early teens through 4-H activities.  In the early 1980’s Janie and Howard were married.  At the time, Howard had 20 head of Suffolk sheep and Janie owned 20 head of Charolais cross cows.  Once married, both became focused on growing the business together, stewarding the land and caring for the livestock.  Howard worked at various auto shops and dealerships while working nights and weekend to build their herd.  In 2000, he opened his own auto repair shop with his brother which he sold in 2010, allowing him to work on the ranch full time.
Meanwhile, Janie received her Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture Education from CSU.  After Howard and Janie moved home to Mesa County she worked for several big box retailers, including as Store Manager when Barnes & Noble opened in Grand Junction.  In 2004, Janie opened her own business, Nick-N-Willy’s Pizza.  The pizza shop was sold in 2015, allowing her to join Howard and work at VanWinkle Ranch full time.
It only took 35 years for the goal to work together to be reached!
A new addition joined the VanWinkle Ranch in the late 1990’s when their only child was born.  Since birth, Dean has been an integral part of the ranch.  He started building his own cow herd through 4-H when he was 8 years old.   Dean graduated from Kansas State University in 2021, when he returned to the ranch.  His wife, Tayler, joined him in 2022.  Paisley, their daughter, will be the 6th generation on the ranch in western Colorado.
The VanWinkle Family continues to be committed to producing affordable, safe and nutritious beef while ensuring there is an abundance of care for the land and community they call home.  VanWinkle Ranch is open to hearing from consumers interested in learning more about how beef is produced and to answer questions.  Please join in the journey by following along with VanWinkle Ranch on facebook.

name: Wing Shack Enterprises, Inc.
notes:
We would like to use the Colorado Proud logo on our sauce bottles
________________
From its start in a tiny shack back in 2004, Wing Shack grew through a dedication to the perfect chicken wing, good karma, and a whole lot of duct tape. What began as a simple idea—serving up crispy wings with unforgettable sauces—quickly turned into something more, thanks to the loyalty of wing lovers and a commitment to create a sense of community with our team and our guests. One location turned into two, then three, then many more. Each new Shack carried the same values: serve great food, treat people well, and stay connected to the communities that made it all possible. Through every expansion, every leap of faith, and every deep fryer hauled into place, the heart of Wing Shack remained the same. Today, it’s a family of 14 restaurants—spanning from as far south as Boulder to as far north as Cheyenne.

What a long strange saucy trip it’s been….

As we continue to grow, we have made a promise to never lose sight of our number one priority: serving the highest quality of food with a genuine appreciation for every customer that visits us.

At the Wing Shack we pride ourselves on the preparation of the chicken wing. We use fresh, never frozen wings and each order is cooked fresh with just the right amount of crispiness. But what is the chicken wing without being tossed in some mouthwatering sauce? We have 16 hand crafted sauces and dry rubs to choose from, ranging from a kid friendly mild sauce to our taste bud incinerating Bear Hot sauce. Every sauce we serve is made from our own original recipes—crafted to ignite flavor and satisfy cravings.. Using only the finest ingredients and freshest peppers, we like to think our sauces are what separates our chicken wings from the rest of the pack.

Our wings might have put us on the map but we take as much pride in our entire menu as we do our wings. Our menu contains an eclectic mix of handhelds and  retro fab chicken nuggets to salads and starters, all cooked fresh to order. And if you aren’t a fan of the traditional wing, don’t worry boo – we got your back with the finest boneless wings tossed however you fancy. But enough talking about it… check our menu yourself and maybe even place an order online here!

Whether you are popping in for a quick lunch or needing thousands of wings for an epic party, know that your order will be prepared fresh and crafted with wing love. No order is too big, no sauce is too spicy, and no wing is too delicious at the Wing Shack.

After twenty years of hot wings and cold beer, all we can say is the future is delicious.

name: Cannolo Family Farms
notes:
From Farm to Fork, Elevate Every Dish with Cannolo Family Farms' Chef-Driven Mushrooms!
Welcome to Cannolo Family Farms, where a passion for culinary excellence meets sustainable farming. Nestled in the scenic heart of Sedalia, Colorado, we are a family-operated mushroom farm dedicated to cultivating the finest gourmet mushrooms.

With deep roots in the restaurant industry, our journey began with a shared love for food and a vision to grow exceptional mushrooms that inspire creativity in kitchens everywhere. From chefs crafting masterpieces to home cooks elevating everyday meals, our mushrooms bring earthy goodness to every table.

At Cannolo Family Farms, we prioritize sustainability and innovation. By combining traditional farming wisdom with modern techniques, we produce mushrooms that are as environmentally conscious as they are delicious. We are committed to nurturing the land, fostering community connections, and contributing to a healthier, more sustainable future.

Join us in celebrating the art of growing and the joy of sharing fresh, high-quality mushrooms with the world. Together, we cultivate for the table, for the earth, and for generations to come.

name: La Dolce Vita Ranch
notes: We are a working family ranch in the high Montagne region of central Colorado. We raise grass-fed/grass-finished cattle and sheep using regenerative practices with land stewardship and animal health and welfare as priorities. We work under an agroecological framework to conserve and even improve the native ecology and wildlife habitat sharing our grazing lands. Rancher Giovanni, originally from Italy, is a multigeneration agrarian and craftsman, who has a knack for hospitality and keeps the ranch going round. Rancher Anna Clare is a rangeland ecosystem scientist and ranch consultant who puts her expertise into practice at La Dolce Vita. We are also horse(wo)men, avid nature-lovers, and have extensive experience camping, hiking, trail riding, and hunting in the Colorado Rockies! In addition to selling our meats and eggs direct to consumer, we host eco-tourism experiences with on-ranch accommodations through AirBnB and Landtrust.com.

name: John  H Heermann Farms
notes: We are a regenerative farm that has followed soil health principles for the last 10 years.  We believe in rejuvenating and restoring the soil and in return the soil provides what is necessary to our crops.  We keep our soil covered, and our below ground ecosystem fed year round.  We save and clean our own seeds on our farm, and use are in house cleaning service.  Utilizing an "old" 1955 Wooden Clipper to clean our grains, and then using a state of the art color sorter to finalize cleaning of our berries to provide the cleanest product of grain.  These grains can be confidently used for sprouting, milling, or feeding.  We utilize older varieties like Turkey Red, and Scout 66 which boast high falling rates, and high protein.  They are also grown chemically free and in a healthy soil which we feel like provides a superior product.

name: Fort Lewis College-Old Fort at Hesperus
notes:
The Old Fort at Hesperus is the original site of Fort Lewis, Fort Lewis Indian School, Fort Lewis High School and Fort Lewis College, located 16 miles southwest of Durango and just south of Hesperus. The  6,318 acres are owned by the Colorado State Land Board and managed by Fort Lewis College. It is a working ranch that has 120 head of mother cows and 400 acres of hay production.
The Old Fort at Hesperus is one of the few educational farms specializing in high-elevation desert farming training, these programs are uniquely positioned to support farmers wishing to work in arid mountain environments. Welcoming everyone from college interns for brief summer experiences to incubator farmers ready to start a business, the Old Fort offers good (and challenging) growing conditions, supportive staff, and diverse resources for high elevation market farming.
We have a on-site Country Store with our vegetables and grass-fed beef along with local pork, lamb, honey, fremont beans, eggs and value added products including dehydrated meals, apple chips, CO Beef sticks and an assortment of lotions and soaps made by our friends and neighbors. name: Lenz Family Farms
notes:
Lenz Farms is a diversified multi-generational crop and livestock farm that operates out of Wray, Colorado.    Together, along with fifteen full time employees, we farm irrigated sand hills farm land, dry land ground and run cattle on prime sand hill grassland.  Crops grown include: corn, wheat, edible beans and potatoes.  The potato operation, Lenz Family Farms, is enhanced by a wash and packing shed that allows us to provide a complete line of gold potatoes for re-packers and retailers across the nation.  Lenz Farms also owns and operates a 2500 head feedlot under the name, Legacy Feeders, LLC.

The unique difference of Lenz Farms is that all partners are working partners that have day to day responsibilities.  From checking sprinklers to fixing equipment, you can find any of the partners with their hands dirty and their wheels turning.  During harvest, ”busy”, is an understatement.  Harvesters, trucks, combines, tractors, the wash shed, and the office are humming along at a brisk pace, trying to beat the weather and winter.  However, even when things are busy, we all try to make time for anyone who drops in with a question or a request.  “PEOPLE ARE OUR PRIORITY” is more than a slogan, it is the reason that we do what we do!

name: Nordic Fox Farm LLC
notes:
Welcome! We’re Mike and Sara Neil and we’re homesteaders growing and living off-grid on 42 beautiful acres just south of Crawford, Colorado. Our time is happily filled with the work of building our dream life here. On any given day you can find us growing medicinal and culinary herbs to share with you, stewarding at-risk plant populations, spending time with our animals, building our home, and creating gorgeous pieces of art. We strive to create seasonal, small-batch products to enhance your life as well as unique home goods to decorate your space.
We also produce the Tending Seeds podcast which covers a wide range of topics about gardening, homesteading, and herbalism.
Sara has completed a 1000 hour certificate in herbalism from the Chestnut School of Herbal Medicine and continues to pursue new paths of learning and study with her peers and elders. Plant conservation and plant medicine accessibility are both passions of hers, and because of that she is a member of United Plant Savers and Herbalists Without Borders. She also served on the leadership board for the Tennessee chapter of the American Herbalists Guild from 2018 until moving to Colorado at the end of 2022. 
Mike has been creating and inventing since he was a teenager and holds several manufacturing patents. A machinist by trade, he has also fallen in love with woodworking in more recent years. He is constantly innovating and improving all of the many moving pieces of our homestead, figuring out how to accomplish our goals using repurposed materials wherever he can and streamlining our farming efforts.

 Beyond gardening, we grow our own organic produce on our quarter acre From Scratch Farm, which we use to craft unforgettable meals through our catering services. name: Marc Arnusch Farms
notes:
Following in the footsteps of his father and grandfather, immigrants to the United States from Austria in 1952, Marc Arnusch became the third generation of Arnusch descendants to work and cultivate land located beneath the shadows of the Rocky Mountains. Today this unique farming community known as Prospect Valley is where Arnusch Farms continues to thrive joined by the 4th generation, Marc and Jill’s son, Brett. 

Our valley enjoys highly productive soils and lies directly on top of the Lost Creek groundwater basin which allows Arnusch Farms to utilize this water resource to irrigate the 2,000-acre land base. The core of the farming operation is centered around cereal grain production, including certified seed barley, seed wheat, and wheat and barley for the thriving Colorado craft brew and distilling industry. Grain corn, corn silage, grain sorghum, and alfalfa round out our production.

At Arnusch Farms, we are committed to growing sustainable, high-quality crops through innovative technologies, meticulous work, resiliency, and the true passion of a generational family operation. It’s this commitment that has driven our family for generations, and it’s this value that will always be at the core of our business.

name: No-MaTer Sauce Company LLC
notes:
No-MaTer Sauce Company LLC is a brand new Colorado-based startup bringing to market tomato-free sauces that taste delicious!
In late 2016 my husband found that he had developed a tomato allergy. The days of BBQ ribs, lasagna, spaghetti, and even fries dipped in a delicious tomato-based fry sauce seemed to be over.
Taste is such a huge part of life that I decided to see what we could do to mix it up. There HAD to be a way to mimic the zesty yumminess that a tomato brings to a dish without causing him distress. 
Now, after two years of experimentation and another couple years of figuring out how to market a product and start a business, I have launched my first product: No-MaTer Marinara Sauce!
This sauce's base is carrots and beets, two super foods, but has a unique blend of spices so as to meld the flavors to trick the tastebuds into believing it is a normal tomato-based marinara sauce. Even the appearance, through no additives, looks like a regular marinara sauce.
With no preservatives added, healthier and simpler ingredients, and nightshade free, No-MaTer Marinara Sauce can bring tomato-like flavor back to those of us who avoid tomatoes for any number of reasons: allergy, auto-immune, and even acid reflux due to tomato.

name: Circle of 2 Ranch
notes:
The Circle of 2 Ranch located in Montrose Colorado is selling PRIME Akaushi beef in quarters, halves or whole. 
About the Akaushi breed. In 1994, the Akaushi breed was brought to the United States from Japan. Not to be confused with Wagyu, which simple means Japanese cattle, Akaushi is a separate and distinct breed. The Akaushi breed started with the South Korean breed known as Hanwoo. Around 1870, the Devon breed was infused into the Hanwoo cattle and around 1910 Simmental was incorporated into the breed. Then around that same time, the breed was closed to any other outside genetics and the Akaushi breed was formed. To this day, Akaushi remains the same, closed herd for well over 100 years.
The Circle of 2 Ranch is a proud member of the American Akaushi Association (AAA). All our cattle are registered with AAA and are FULL-BLOOD Akaushi. We currently have three herd bulls that are descendants of "Big Al". We have on our ranch: Mac Daddy, Oden, and Taco Cat. Our Akaushi are born and raised on our ranch in Montrose on the Western Slope of Colorado. Our animals never leave the property, not for one minute, until they are fully finished and ready for the consumer. We call it "estate beef". The calves wean naturally from their mothers, their horns are left intact, and moving the herd from one grazing field to another is a process free of poking and prodding. We steer our bulls and hand feed them twice a day a diet of grass and work with an animal nutritionist for our special finishing blend. They are fed out for an impressive 300 days! Unlike most American beef operations in which calves are sold off to growers and feedlots to plump up on a mostly corn diet, the cows at the Circle of 2 Ranch eat a variety of grasses for their entire lives on the ranch. They also have access to a free-flowing creek of fresh water that runs through the ranch. This guarantees a PRIME grading of A5 beef. They are handled daily and enjoy a relaxing, stress-free environment. These animals are antibiotic and hormone free! So you get this amazing, moist, well-marbled beef with a flavor that you just don’t get in any other situation, because [the cows] having fed on these grasses gives a density and almost a minerality to the meat. And the fat in grass-fed beef has a higher omega-3 content than non-grass-fed beef. It melts at a much lower temperature, so it’s literally melting in your mouth. We rotate the animals on the grass so that they’re actually part of the tilling and regeneration of the field.

At Quarter Circle Kunekunes we strive to conserve the Kunekune breed of pig based on conformation, structure, and appropriate growth rate for pork production. Our docile pigs are raised in a herd setting on quality grass pasture.

Our farm is located on the Western Slope of Colorado outside of Montrose. We currently have five pasture raised breeding quality Kunekune sows and three pasture raised breeding quality Kunekune boars. We often have 20-30 pasture raised barrows and piglets alongside future Kunekune breeding prospects.

All of our breeding Kunekunes are registered through the International Kunekune Hog Registry (formally the American Kunekune Pig Registry) and all piglets are IKHR/AKPR litter notified. We believe in pedigreed pure stock guaranteed by DNA testing. We are breeding these pastured pigs to do our part with the improvement and conservation of Kunekune pigs in the United States, which includes pedigreed pastured pork production. 

We believe in respecting and honoring all living beings on our farm; this does not exclude our pork pigs. We emphasize compassion and respect for all stages of the life cycle and hold the highest regard for our meat animals. None of us is classically trained in wine making, and that’s nothing we’re ashamed of.  As a matter of fact, we embrace it; it’s a point of pride; it’s an opportunity to be ourselves even in our wines, to take risks we see as practical that others see as crazy. name: Bingo Burger
notes:
Pueblo, Colorado sits smack-dab in the middle of Colorado’s high desert. Its climate is perfect for growing the namesake Pueblo Chile. Long hot days and an abundance of sunshine and cool nights result in a spicy, sweet and robust chile pepper. Pueblo Chiles, beloved by locals and gaining popularity nationwide, are what give the signature Bingo Burger its special quality… they’re mixed right in with choice Colorado ground beef!

The Bingo Burger was launched during Pueblo’s Annual Chile & Frijole Festival in 2007. Chef/Owner Richard Warner set up a grill in front of his wife’s Hopscotch Bakery and grilled hundreds of burgers for folks hungry for something different. He capitalized on the unique flavor of the locally-grown and roasted Pueblo chile and mixed them right into the beef before grilling. BINGO! The Bingo Burger was born. These burgers proved to be so popular that a brick and mortar shop opened its doors in 2009 in the heart of Pueblo’s Downtown District. A few years later we headed up north to stake our claim to Colorado Springs.

Burgers and fries cooked to order, creamy milkshakes and malts and icy, cold Colorado craft beers all served in a fun and funky atmosphere make Bingo Burger a winner with locals and out-of-towners alike!

name: Patterson Pastures
notes:
We are Patterson Pastures. Ranch raised beef and pork from our pasture to your table. We raise beef and pork on our small ranch in eastern Colorado. We believe that now more than ever, it is important to know where your food comes from. You need to make sure that it is safe, healthy to eat, tasty, and……..available. 

With recent events in mind, and after experiencing shortages in the grocery stores we decided to shift our focus to a farm to table operation and sell direct to the consumer. 

We look forward to serving you and are humbled that you will give us an opportunity to serve you. We do not want to take business away from another family farm who you may be trading with now, but if your only source for meat is the grocery store, we ask that you give us a try to earn your business.

name: Douglas Creek Enterprises LLC dba Douglas Creek Tallow
notes:
Douglas Creek Tallow, a subsidiary of Douglas Creek Enterprises, LLC, is a locally owned, operated and produced, skin and hair care business. At Douglas Creek Tallow, we honor the traditions of natural skincare. Each creation begins with nature’s purest sourced tallow, enriched by botanicals and crafted in small batches. From our pristine pastures to your daily skincare, we bring you the essence of natural beauty. Our mission is: Pure ingredients. Refined formulations. Uncompromising results. 

I’m a fifth generation Western CO rancher. I own and operate a cow/calf ranch in Rangely, CO. The tallow will be sourced locally from my ranch and other local ranchers and crafted by me. This company is a small family business  consisting of me, mom, Jessica Potter, and my two young daughters, Paisley and Lillie who are on the verge of their teen years. The idea was created due to their acute interest in skincare and beauty products. Beef suet is an underutilized byproduct. We have found a value-added way to not only utilize more of the beef carcasses we  and local ranchers produce, but to create a highly demanded, locally sourced and produced new product. 

The business is still in startup phase. We currently don’t have social media or websites up and going yet. We are hoping to get all the labeling (including CO proud membership) finalized prior to going live with product sales.

name: Half Section Plus, LLC
notes:
Half Section Plus, LLC is a small, hands‑on farm in Colorado, focused on real pasture‑raised eggs from a healthy, mixed flock of laying hens. Our chickens spend their days outside roaming grass, scratching for bugs and seeds, and soaking up sunshine, not standing in cages or cramped barns.

That active, forage‑rich lifestyle shows up in the carton: firm whites, rich golden yolks, and sturdy shells that hold up well in your kitchen. We gather every egg by hand and lightly dry‑clean when needed, then leave the natural protective “bloom” (cuticle) on the shell so the egg stays sealed and naturally guarded from bacteria the way the hen designed it.

Our eggs are a good fit for customers looking for local, pasture‑raised food and who appreciate knowing exactly where their breakfast came from. We’re proud to offer fresh, honest eggs from birds that are raised with care on real Colorado pasture.

Schedule and pickup instructions
Egg pickup is by appointment only at Half Section Plus, LLC. Monday–Friday, pickups are available from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, and Saturdays from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm. No Sunday pickup is available.

To schedule a pickup time, please text 720‑933‑2289 or email halfsectionplus@gmail.com and wait for confirmation before coming to the farm. No eggs are sold without an appointment.

On your appointment day, park in the designated egg pickup parking area just off the public road, then send a quick text to let us know you’ve arrived. We will drive out to your vehicle and hand‑deliver your eggs so you do not need to leave your car.

All sales are cash only at this time. Please bring exact change when possible.

name: Winters  Ranch

Our Story
We are 5th generation Colorado Cattle Ranchers located in Rush Colorado. We take great pride in raising high-quality Black Angus beef. It takes 2 years for a Beef to be ready for butcher.

During the winter months, our cattle receive feed high-quality feed, hay, cattle cubs minerals, and Salt. We care greatly for our animals and want them to live a happy, healthy, natural life. We do not pen up our cattle. They are on grass until they go to butcher. This helps with the quality and flavor of the meat.

When it's ready for your table, we offer high-quality dry-aged beef. Once you taste how good our beef is we can promise you will not buy from a grocery store again. 🇺🇸 Thank you for supporting your local Ranchers!

name: Colorado Farm to Table
notes: Get involved in growing produce, relationships, and community! At Salida’s not-for-profit Colorado Farm to Table (CFTT) we grow approximately 10 acres of fresh produce for distribution to Coloradans in need. Starting in 2022, we are going to have a separate 1 acre plot of fresh vegetables to sell at the farmers market with all proceeds going back to our donation farm. The summer of 2022 will be our 26th season, CFTT has been welcoming people of all backgrounds in volunteer farming experiences to grow top-quality, nutritious produce for hungry families. Volunteer farm hands work with the farmer in 3-hour shifts. No experience is necessary – instruction and tools are provided. Join us! It’s a lot of fun and a great opportunity to meet and network with some awesome people. CFTT’s sustainably grown produce is distributed via partner nonprofit food pantries, soup kitchens, low-income housing, and feeding programs that redistribute the freshly harvested produce onto the plates of those most in need of nutrition relief. We encourage and welcome new volunteers, distribution partners, and innovative collaborative partnerships. Contact info@coloradofarmtotable.org for more information!

We are driven by a commitment to cultivate a future built upon the values of integrity and respect passed down through our lineage, all while strengthening the community around us.

Our philosophy centers on enabling our cattle to flourish in their intended environment. They spend their days freely grazing on 400 acres of diverse native grasses near Sterling, benefiting from the open air and sunshine. This natural upbringing not only fosters their healthy development but also imbues the beef with exceptional nutritional value and inherent, delicious flavor. A vital part of our promise is that our cattle are never given antibiotics or hormones. This dedication to pure, responsible farming ensures a healthier product for your table and reflects our deep respect for each animal. Avoiding antibiotics helps in the broader effort to combat resistance, and foregoing hormones supports their natural growth cycle.

For the final 60 days, we transition to a carefully managed "grain finishing" phase using a non-GMO corn feed. This controlled period is essential for achieving the perfect balance of tenderness and the rich, desirable flavor that complements the excellent quality developed on pasture. We are confident this balanced approach delivers the finest product: outstanding nutrition, remarkable taste, and complete assurance in the quality of your food.

As caretakers of this precious environment, our herd, and the natural rhythm of life on the farm, we embrace this significant responsibility with sincere gratitude. Sharing the result of our diligent work with you – beef raised with ultimate care, respect, and an unwavering standard for quality – is a source of genuine joy for us.

name: Flying B Bar Ranch
notes:
Flying B Bar Ranch, located in Strasburg, Colorado, is a second-generation ranch that produces grass fed grass finished Wagyu/Angus cattle and Natural Heritage Pork, and is the passion pursuit of the Buchanan family; Brad, Margaret, Grace and Will and Partner Zach Angotti. 

At Flying B Bar Ranch, our cattle are 100% grass fed and finished. This means no grains, corn, or soy, ever, during their entire lives, and we never use hormones, antibiotics, or steroids.  They get nothing but grass and sunshine, while roaming on thousands of acres of natural prairie grasses. We use holistically planned grazing, utilizing rotational and intensive grazing techniques. In short, our cattle are constantly moving from pasture to pasture throughout the year based upon weather, soil and grass conditions. This ensures each pasture the adequate recovery time and keeps cattle moving how they were naturally meant to. This gives our cattle plenty of nutrition, exercise, and grass, while protecting the natural ecosystem from overgrazing and losing nutrients and moisture in the soil. Our cattle walk the land and churn the earth with their hooves, breaking down debris and fertilizing the soil. Cattle can be THE best tool for conserving and improving soil and grass health if done correctly! 

We are certified by the American Grassfed Association as 100% grass fed and finished. Their certification is the gold standard in regenerative ranching, and it means you can buy our beef with confidence that we raised our cattle the right way, rather than the fast way. We give our cattle plenty of room to roam and graze, and plenty of time to be themselves. We stand by our practices, and unlike the Wizard of Oz, we are happy to pull back the curtain and show our customers exactly how we do what we do, and why we do it the way we do it.  

We focus on the soil because that creates better grass, and better grass makes for better cattle and a better planet. We build our soil and its nutrients by planting cover crops, encouraging native wildlife and birds, and working with the land, rather than against it. That’s why we ranch the way we do; to create a natural balance that nourishes the earth, the cattle, and our customers. The natural prairie grasses of eastern Colorado have evolved over millions of years to be efficient at storing water and carbon in the soil, and our entire operation revolves around giving those grasses every opportunity to succeed. We do this not just because it’s the right thing to do, but because it’s good business too: every year that our pastures can store more water, carbon, and nutrients means that the next year the prairie will be stronger, grow better, and support more of our natural ecosystem. This means we can support more cattle, who can then support more pasture and prairie. It’s a cycle, and we work hard to take care of it. 

We love what we do, and we are dedicated to educating the public about the benefits of knowing where your food comes from and supplying them with food that they can trust. 

Learn more at www.flyingbbar.com
